title: Mật độ đô thị · Discuss both views
prompt: Some people support encouraging high-density housing around public transport stations, while others oppose it because of the risks it could create. Discuss both views and give your own opinion.
instructions: Give reasons for your answer and include any relevant examples from your own knowledge or experience. Write at least 250 words.

paragraphs: Housing near stations links decisions about urban growth to the number of people who can use public transport conveniently. I support high-density housing around stations, provided planning also secures affordable homes, schools and usable public space for the growing population.

Supporters argue that compact development can shorten journeys and support viable public transport. A larger population within walking distance creates regular demand without requiring extensive parking. Apartments near a station could reduce dependence on a second household car. Concentrated demand can support frequent services, creating a practical link between land use and transport viability that scattered development may struggle to achieve.

Opponents warn that density without adequate schools and open space can reduce everyday liveability. Concentrating homes also concentrates demand for schools, public space and local services. If these are not expanded, shorter travel can come with overcrowded facilities, while rising land values may exclude the lower-income households expected to benefit most from convenient transport. Planning should coordinate housing with services, green areas and affordable access. Coordinated provision needs schools, public space and affordable homes, so concentrating residents does not merely move the bottleneck from roads to other essential services. Developers and local authorities should agree school places and pedestrian access before homes are occupied, so the first residents do not spend years waiting for facilities promised in planning documents. Shorter journeys and stronger demand for trains can benefit residents daily, but overcrowded schools or displacement can absorb those gains unless services and affordability grow with housing.

In conclusion, station-area density merits priority as coordinated neighbourhood development: better transport access must remain affordable and should not be purchased through deteriorating schools or public space.
